evidence.excerpt: The heat transfer coefficient (HTC) between polymer melt and mould steel during the filling and packing stages is a poorly characterised boundary condition that strongly influences warpage predictions. This study systematically varied the interfacial HTC from 1000 to 10 000 W/m²K in a commercial process simulation environment for a PA6 box-shaped part (80 × 60 × 30 mm, 2.5 mm wall) and quantified the resulting spread in predicted warpage and residual stress distributions. Warpage at the open rim varied by up to 0.38 mm (factor of 2.4) over the HTC range, whereas residual stresses at mid-wall varied by less than 6%. An inverse identification procedure using CMM warpage measurements from 20 experimental parts at two mould temperatures was used to back-calculate effective HTC values. Identified HTC values were 2 400 ± 310 W/m²K at 40 °C mould temperature and 1 850 ± 260 W/m²K at 70 °C mould temperature. Recommendations for standardising HTC calibration in simulation workflows are given.
